 California 2026 Poll: Xavier Becerra Holds 27-Point Lead over Steve Hilton
 October 21st, 2026
 Home Polls California 2026 Poll: Xavier Becerra Holds 27-Point Lead over Steve Hilton 
 Gov. Newsom Holds 46% Approval, 43% Disapproval Rating 
 A new Emerson College Polling survey of California voters finds Democrat Xavier Becerra with a 27-point lead over Republican Steve Hilton, 60% to 33%. Seven percent are undecided. After undecided voters are asked which candidate they lean toward, Becerra leads 64% to 36%.
 “After receiving the plurality of votes in the open primary for Governor with 28% in June, Becerra leads Hilton in the race for Governor, outside the survey’s margin of error,” Spencer Kimball, executive director of Emerson College Polling, said. “California independents break for Becerra by 10 points, 46% to 36%, a group Hilton would need more support among to compete in the general election.”
 The economy is the top issue for 45% of California voters, along with housing affordability (17%), healthcare (10%), and immigration (10%).
 When asked who they think is responsible for the current state of the California economy, 44% say President Trump, 38% Governor Newsom, 7% the Republican majority in Congress, and 8% someone else. 
 Compared to a year ago , the percentage of voters who blame President Trump for the state of the California economy increased 17 points, from 27% to 44%, while those who blame Newsom decreased 13 points, from 51% to 38%.
 President Trump holds a 33% approval rating; 63% disapprove of the job Trump is doing in office. Governor Gavin Newsom holds a 46% job approval rating, and 43% disapproval. Twelve percent are neutral.
 Methodology 
 The Emerson College Polling California survey was conducted October 17-19, 2026. The overall sample of California likely voters, n=1,000, has a credibility interval, similar to a poll’s margin of error (MOE), of +/- 3.1 percent. The data sets were weighted by gender, education, party registration, and region based on U.S. Census parameters and voter file data. 
 It is important to remember that subsets based on demographics, such as gender, age, education, and race/ethnicity, carry with them higher credibility intervals, as the sample size is reduced. Survey results should be understood within the poll’s range of scores, and with a confidence interval of 95% a poll will fall outside the range of scores 1 in 20 times. 
 Data was collected by contacting registered voters from a voter file provided by Aristotle using MMS text-to-web, probability-based panel of voters provided by Consensus Strategies using MMS text-to-web, additional panel interviews were provided by PureSpectrum. All respondents were recruited using customized links that prevent responses from anyone outside of the poll’s sample frame. Panel responses were matched to the Aristotle voter file using respondents’ full name and ZIP code. The survey was administered using QuestionPro.
